html:
A nerve gas attack on the Tokyo subway on 20 March 1995 by members of the cult Aum Shinrikyo. During the morning rush hour they punctured bags of liquid sarin on five trains on three lines that passed under the government district.

Fourteen people died in the end and thousands were hurt, some for life. It was the worst attack on Japan's soil since the Second World War.

Aum was led by Shoko Asahara, who mixed Buddhist and Hindu ideas with prophecies of the end of the world. The cult had recruited educated young people, including scientists, and had already killed opponents and carried out a smaller sarin attack in Matsumoto in 1994. Police raids followed the subway attack, and Asahara was arrested in May 1995. He and twelve followers were executed in 2018.

Coming two months after the Kobe earthquake, and in the gloom after the asset bubble burst, the attack shook the sense of safety in Japan.
